headline: Proteomics search spaces widen to proteoforms, modifications, and coverage gaps
label: Proteomics Search Space Expansion
summary: Expanded search spaces now reach dark-proteome spectra and proteoforms, while peptide coverage bias in public data is measured explicitly.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the expansion of what proteomics searches can assign, paired with explicit checks on what those assignments cover. π-SPECFormer, pre-trained on 291M spectra, targets dark-proteome decoding through de novo sequencing, spectrum clustering and modification detection. mE-DIA combines multi-enzyme, library-free DIA-MS with proteoform inference and a peptide mapper, reporting a 30% gain in protein identifications and more resolved proteoforms. On the constraint side, SeekNSee prioritizes proteotypic peptides via enzyme-aware in silico digestion with traceable rule-level scoring. A proteoform-aware reanalysis of public bottom-up evidence finds basic-pI peptides depleted (OR 0.45). msiFlow 2.0 is less directly aligned, extending imaging workflows with recalibration, lipid annotation, ComBat batch correction and QC. What is new is the joint move toward proteoform-level resolution and measured coverage gaps, with scoring rules made traceable.
